latin_incipit: Deus movet primum coelum non solum ut causa finalis, sed etiam ut verus agens et proprius motor.
english_translation: God moves the first heaven not only as final cause, but also as true efficient and proper mover.
charge: Pico (citing Averroes) rejects Aristotle's account of the Unmoved Mover as merely a final cause, asserting God's role as efficient cause.
defense: This upholds divine agency and active causation, more in keeping with Neoplatonic and Christian theology.
exegesis: Against Aristotle's 'unmoved mover' as merely a final cause, Pico (citing Averroes) affirms God is an efficient cause—a real mover of the cosmos. This leans toward a more personalistic theism.

scholar_citations.quote: The Unmoved Mover is a final cause, moving all things by being an object of desire and thought.
God must be understood as both final and efficient cause of all motion, not merely as an object of desire.

scholar_citations.work: Summa Theologiae, Prima Pars, Q. 2-3 (proofs of God's existence and causation)
scholar_citations.quote: God is the ultimate efficient cause of all being and motion in the cosmos.
scholar_citations.source_note: [Christian synthesis of efficient and final causation]

scholar_citations.work: The Arabic Influences on Early Modern Occult Philosophy
scholar_citations.quote: This shift to efficient causation in God allowed Renaissance magicians to conceptualize celestial influence as active transmission of form and virtue.
scholar_citations.source_note: [Saif on God as efficient cause in magical cosmology]

notes: Critical for Pico's theology of divine action and his justification of astral magic as part of God's active governance of creation.
